items.title: Royal Caribbean Moves Onto Land With $3 Billion Deal for Half of Sandals
items.summary: The Caribbean's biggest cruise company now co-owns its best-known resort brand, betting that cruise guests and resort guests are the same customer.

items.title: As Adani Eyes Airline Entry, India Weighs ‘Pros and Cons’ of Letting Airport Operators Own Carriers
items.summary: India wants to break the airline duopoly. It now has to decide whether giving airport operators a seat in the cockpit is the way to do it.

items.title: F1’s Bahrain Shuffle Turns October Into a Southeast Asia Hotel Boom
items.summary: Bahrain’s move to Malaysia creates an F1 doubleheader with Singapore — and a chance for hotels to turn two race weekends into one regional travel surge.

items.title: Sri Lanka Wants 3 Million Tourists. It’s More Interested in What They Spend
items.summary: Sri Lanka wants more tourists, of course. But these days, it is keeping a close eye on not just how many arrive, but what they are worth beyond the arrival count.

items.title: Why Brand USA Can’t Market the NFL
items.summary: Destinations can capitalize on hosting a Super Bowl, World Cup, or Olympics — but DMOs are often constrained to marketing around the event, not through it.

items.title: ‘The Traveler Comes to Us’: Uber CEO Explains Break-Even Bet on Hotels
items.summary: Uber wants to be more than just a rideshare company. Speaking at the Skift Global Forum, Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said the company is expanding into hotels and short-term rental bookings. Flights could be a possibility too.

items.title: That Creator Video Went Viral, the Booking Came Later: How Brands Measure Impact
items.summary: The path from online inspiration to booking isn’t linear. Travel brands say measurement is all about "incrementality."

items.title: How Travel Brands Learned to Stop Worrying and Trust Creators
items.summary: Travel brands are letting go of the curated campaigns and heavily produced videos in favor of giving more creative control to creators.
